task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req176-dlq-core.md against every REQ-176 acceptance criterion. Specifically: (1) read Letflow.Tasks.list_tasks/2's actual keyset-cursor implementation (or whatever module the design cites) and confirm the design's claimed cursor prefix/encoding/ordering scheme genuinely mirrors an existing, working pattern rather than a plausible-sounding invention; (2) read Letflow.Tasks.claim_task/3 (or cited equivalent) and confirm the row-lock-then-check-then-conditionally-write idiom is real and applies cleanly to retry/2 and discard/2's two-arm state checks; (3) read Letflow.IdentityMigration's cited text-cast ILIKE pattern and confirm it's real; (4) confirm the schema design (status as a closed Ecto.Enum with lowercase values, entry_type as a plain :string not enum, retry_history as a plain jsonb array not embeds_many) is internally consistent and matches DlqEntry/DlqRetryAttempt field-for-field, cross-checking web/src/types/api.ts yourself; (5) confirm no fenced code block anywhere in the document reproduces real .ex content or writes out actual Ecto schema/migration/query syntax as fact rather than prose description; (6) confirm the three flagged open questions (tenant_id sourcing into enqueue/1, whether retry/2 consults retry_limit, whether retry/2 advances last_failed_at) don't hide an acceptance-criterion gap -- none of REQ-176's 6 ACs actually require resolving them, but double check; (7) confirm no route/controller design is present anywhere (that's REQ-178's scope).
acceptance_criteria: the dlq_entries table lives inside each tenant's Postgres schema with a tenant_id column retained, matching decision 0003 Decision B's pattern -- verified by inspecting the migration

enqueue/1 creates an entry with status "pending", retry_count 0, and a created_at timestamp; list/2 is tenant-scoped, demonstrated by an entry enqueued under tenant A being absent from a list/2 call scoped to tenant B

retry/2 on a "pending" or "retrying" entry transitions it to "retrying", appends a retry_history entry with attempt_no/attempted_at/outcome/error_message field names matching DlqRetryAttempt exactly, and increments retry_count; retry/2 on a "resolved" or "discarded" entry returns a conflict error and leaves status, retry_count and retry_history unchanged -- four tests, one per starting status
discard/2 on a "pending" or "retrying" entry transitions it to "discarded"; discard/2 on an already "resolved" or "discarded" entry returns a conflict error rather than silently succeeding

list/2 filters by entry_type and by status independently, each demonstrated narrowing a result set that contains rows of more than one value, and supports cursor pagination: given more rows than one page, the first page's next_cursor, passed back in, returns the next distinct page with no repeated or skipped ids
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
